articleTitle: Framework for Voice-controlled AI Teaching Assistant for Specially-abled
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International conference on Artificial Intelligence and Signal Processing (AISP)
abstract: Recent advancements in technology have triggered a revolution in the education sector. One of the significant developments of this change is being granted access to vast online resources from various world class institutes. The motivation behind this paper is to be able to create a technological solution for providing equal opportunities to specially-abled online learners who may have physical disabilities such as visual impairment, loss of hands/weak hand motor skills, etc., and enable their participation for a more inclusive society. The paper uses a twofold approach. Firstly, it provides literature on various state-of-art assistive technologies for e-learning portals. Secondly, the paper proposes a learning framework as teaching assistant for specially-abled, which is artificial intelligence based and interactive voice enabled. The proposed framework has three modules completely controlled by voice commands for self-paced -reading, learning and auto-marking assessment. The assessment module generates fill-in-the-blanks and question-answers, which is a part of continuous comprehensive tests. As a case study, the proposed framework is prototyped on an e-learning platform DIKSHA, which hosts digital books from National Council of Educational Research and Training. Natural language processing toolkit based on Python libraries has been used. The results have been found encouraging. Extensions for future work are also discussed.

articleTitle: Impact of Suitable Wind Speed Prediction in a Competitive Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International conference on Artificial Intelligence and Signal Processing (AISP)
abstract: In recent times power generation is increasing at a higher rate to fulfill the extended power demand throughout the globe. In this scenario, renewable sources provide a considerable amount of power to mitigate the burden on primary energy sources (i.e. thermal power). In a competitive renewable incorporated electrical system, the prediction of renewable power is essential, and need to submit this data to the electricity market at least one day before the operation. Violating the predicted renewable data as compared with real data creates the situation of imposing a penalty/reward (imbalance cost) on the power plant by market controller for not meeting up their power generation which affects the generation company's economic profit. The accurate prediction method of renewable energy can mitigate the negative effect of imbalance cost which will be helpful for the power producer. This paper shows the effect of appropriate wind speed prediction in a competitive power system in terms of system profit and some methodologies have been also suggested here to perform accurate wind speed prediction.

articleTitle: Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis prediction Using Deep Reinforcement Learning on Primary Tumor Biopsy Slides
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International conference on Artificial Intelligence and Signal Processing (AISP)
abstract: The “Sentinel Lymph Node Biopsy” (SLNB) is a common practice for detecting metastasis in Breast Cancer patients. It has improved the accuracy of predicting “Axillary Lymph Node” (ALN) status, allowing some women to avoid “Axillary Lymph Node Dissection” (ALND). However, SLNB is an invasive technique that has the potential to induce problems such as “lymphedema” and numbness in the upper limbs. Furthermore, the frozen segment of the SLNB takes a significant amount of time, which extends the total duration of the surgery. In this research work, a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approach has been used to pre-operatively predict ALN involvement in early-stage Breast Cancer patients using Whole Slide Images (WSIs). The goal was to achieve accurate ALN involvement detection, which is crucial in determining the best treatment options and avoiding unnecessary surgery and related complications. A Convolutional Neural Network model based on Deep Learning was also used for ALN metastasis prediction. The results of the experimentation demonstrate that the DRL algorithm outperformed the CNN model in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, with values of 67.7121%, 65.1499%, 67.7121%, and 63.519% respectively.
